title: CoCoEmo: Composable and Controllable Human-Like Emotional TTS via Activation Steering
claim: Emotion control is achieved by injecting vectors, built from activation mean-differences, into selected layers of the language module of a two-stage pipeline.
layout: 2 regions: inference pipeline left, vector construction right; left-to-right, red steering paths
description: A wide figure split by a dashed vertical line. The left half, titled Inference-Time Steering, has two stages. In the first, a text-to-speech language model takes text embeddings, reference speech tokens and a condition embedding. It runs through a row of transformer layers, and red steering-vector icons mark two of the layers. Red arrows run from a zoomed transformer-layer block at the bottom, which shows the steering equation, up to those layers. Synthesised tokens are generated autoregressively and loop back. In the second stage, a flow-matching module and vocoder turn the tokens and a reference mel into a target mel and then synthesised speech. The right half, Steering Vector Construction, has two parts. The first computes an activation mean-difference between neutral and emotional sets. The second blends two emotion vectors into a mixed vector using weights. A legend runs along the bottom. Colored circles distinguish token types.
caption: Overview of our method. Left: Stage-1: The SLM generates speech tokens; steering vectors are injected at selected layers and operators. Stage-2: Flow-matching and vocoder produce the final waveform. Right: Steering vector construction.
abstract: Emotional expression in human speech is nuanced and compositional, often involving multiple, sometimes conflicting, affective cues that may diverge from linguistic content. In contrast, most expressive text-to-speech systems enforce a single utterance-level emotion, collapsing affective diversity and suppressing mixed or text-emotion-misaligned expression. While activation steering via latent direction vectors offers a promising solution, it remains unclear whether emotion representations are linearly steerable in TTS, where steering should be applied within hybrid TTS architectures, and how such complex emotion behaviors should be evaluated. This paper presents the first systematic analysis of activation steering for emotional control in hybrid TTS models, introducing a quantitative, controllable steering framework, and multi-rater evaluation protocols that enable composable mixed-emotion synthesis and reliable text-emotion mismatch synthesis. Our results demonstrate, for the first time, that emotional prosody and expressive variability are primarily synthesized by the TTS language module instead of the flow-matching module, and also provide a lightweight steering approach for generating natural, human-like emotional speech.
